section.title: org.osgi.util.converter
section.para: Converter Package Version 1.0.

Bundles wishing to use this package must list the package in the Import-Package header of the bundle's manifest. This package has two types of users: the consumers that use the API in this package and the providers that implement the API in this package.

listitem.para: ConversionException - This Runtime Exception is thrown when an object is requested to be converted but the conversion cannot be done.
Converter - The Converter service is used to start a conversion.
ConverterBuilder - A builder to create a new converter with modified behavior based on an existing converter.
ConverterFunction - An functional interface with a convert method that is passed the original object and the target type to perform a custom conversion.
Converters - Factory class to obtain the standard converter or a new converter builder.
Converting - This interface is used to specify the target that an object should be converted to.
Functioning - This interface is used to specify the target function to perform conversions.
Rule - A rule implementation that works by capturing the type arguments via subclassing.
Specifying - This is the base interface for the Converting and Functioning interfaces and defines the common modifiers that can be applied to these.
TargetRule - Interface for custom conversion rules.
TypeReference - An object does not carry any runtime information about its generic type.
TypeRule - Rule implementation that works by passing in type arguments rather than subclassing.

section.title: public class ConversionException extends RuntimeException
section.para: This Runtime Exception is thrown when an object is requested to be converted but the conversion cannot be done. For example when the String "test" is to be converted into a Long.

section.para: Create a Conversion Exception with a message and a nested cause.

section.title: public interface Converter
section.para: The Converter service is used to start a conversion. The service is obtained from the service registry. The conversion is then completed via the Converting interface that has methods to specify the target type.

section.title: public interface ConverterBuilder
section.para: A builder to create a new converter with modified behavior based on an existing converter. The modified behavior is specified by providing rules and/or conversion functions. If multiple rules match they will be visited in sequence of registration. If a rule's function returns null the next rule found will be visited. If none of the rules can handle the conversion, the original converter will be used to perform the conversion.

formalpara.title: Provider Type
formalpara.para: Consumers of this API must not implement this type

section.title: public Converter build()
section.para: Build the specified converter. Each time this method is called a new custom converter is produced based on the rules registered with the builder.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: A new converter with the rules provided to the builder.

section.para: Register a custom error handler. The custom error handler will be called when the conversion would otherwise throw an exception. The error handler can either throw a different exception or return a value to be used for the failed conversion.

formalpara.title: Returns

section.title: public interface ConverterFunction
section.para: An functional interface with a convert method that is passed the original object and the target type to perform a custom conversion.
This interface can also be used to register a custom error handler.

section.title: public static final Object CANNOT_HANDLE
section.para: Special object to indicate that a custom converter rule or error handler cannot handle the conversion.

section.title: public Object apply(Object obj, Type targetType) throws Exception

formalpara.title: obj
formalpara.para: The object to be converted. This object will never be null as the convert function will not be invoked for null values.

section.para: Convert the object into the target type.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: The conversion result or CANNOT_HANDLE to indicate that the convert function cannot handle this conversion. In this case the next matching rule or parent converter will be given a opportunity to convert.

formalpara.title: Throws
formalpara.para: Exception– the operation can throw an exception if the conversion can not be performed due to incompatible types.

section.title: public T extends Specifying<T> view()
section.para: Return a live view over the backing object that reflects any changes to the original object. This is only possible with conversions to java.util.Map, java.util.Collection, java.util.List and java.util.Set. The live view object will cease to be live as soon as modifications are made to it. Note that conversions to an interface or annotation will always produce a live view that cannot be modified. This modifier has no effect with conversions to other types.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: The current Converting object so that additional calls can be chained.

section.title: public class TypeReference<T>

formalpara.title: <T>
formalpara.para: The target type for the conversion.

section.para: An object does not carry any runtime information about its generic type. However sometimes it is necessary to specify a generic type, that is the purpose of this class. It allows you to specify an generic type by defining a type T, then subclassing it. The subclass will have a reference to the super class that contains this generic information. Through reflection, we pick this reference up and return it with the getType() call.

section.title: protected TypeReference()
section.para: A TypeReference cannot be directly instantiated. To use it, it has to be extended, typically as an anonymous inner class.

section.title: public Type getType()
section.para: Return the actual type of this Type Reference
